  "contract": "A derived value is a new, independent thing, and the comparison that decides whether it changed must look exactly as far as the thing it is comparing: a derivation carries forward every property the original carried that the derivation does not deliberately replace (including the caller's overrides and the parts held-but-disregarded), it mints fresh identity for every member it invents wherever identity is what later tells members apart, it tolerates an original produced by an older or sparser writer rather than assuming every field the current writer emits is present, and it is never produced by writing into the object it was handed — and correspondingly, no equality check may declare two values the same on evidence shallower than the level at which they actually differ, nor declare two structurally identical freshly-built values different.",
